title: Canary ejection incident notes
content:
Notes-to-self: messy, fast, still iterating. Goal: capture commands I ran, error outputs, immediate hypotheses, and next steps for clean handoff.

High-level summary:
- Canary for release v2025.02.14 failed at 10% with latency spike and 5% error rate. Automated canary ejection triggered but rollback left some traffic on canary instances. Suspect artifact/digest mismatch + ingress sticky sessions.

Timeline (rough):
- 2025-02-14T10:02 UTC: CI -> build pushed image gcr.io/redwood/release:v2025.02.14-0a1b2c (digest sha256:aa11bb...).
- 2025-02-14T10:10 UTC: deploy job started (deploy/canary-release). Helm chart applied with release tag v2025.02.14.
- 2025-02-14T10:18 UTC: monitoring alerts: canary latency p95 jumped 3x, 5xx increase.
- 2025-02-14T10:21 UTC: auto-eject triggered (traffic scaled back to stable), but traces show ~3 pods still receiving new sessions.

Commands I ran (copyable):
- kubectl -n prod get pods -l release=canary-v2025-02-14 -o wide
  -> showed 5 pods, 2 in CrashLoopBackOff for a short window.
- kubectl logs pod/canary-abc-0 -n prod --since=1h | sed -n '1,200p'
  -> error snippet: "panic: nil pointer deref at kv_cache.go:214" (stack + runtime frames).
- docker pull gcr.io/redwood/release:v2025.02.14-0a1b2c && docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' gcr.io/redwood/release:v2025.02.14-0a1b2c\  -> digest reported sha256:aa11bb..., matches CI build metadata but Helm chart picked image by tag only.
- kubectl describe rs canary-v2025-02-14 -n prod\  -> events: "failed to create pod: image pull backoff" (brief), then recovered.
- kubectl rollout undo deployment/canary-deploy --to-revision=3 -n prod\  -> rollout started; observed mixed images in replicaset (old RS still had some pods).

Observed error snippets (copied):
- "error response from daemon: manifest unknown: manifest unknown" (from node kubelet when trying to pull a very short-lived image pull attempt)
- agent logs: "kv_cache.go:214: assertion failed: expected slice length > 0"
- envoy: "upstream 10.10.20.33:8080 unhealthy (503)"

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Race: CI pushed new image digest but tag was reused (floating tag) and some nodes saw different digests due to regional registry replication latency => mixed artifact digests during canary rollout.
2) Sticky sessions / session affinity + partial traffic ejection: canary pods kept long-lived connections so ejection didn't immediately drain traffic => residual errors.
3) New binary has a latent null-pointer in a rarely-used KV path hit by canary traffic pattern (small batch of users) leading to 5xxs and pod restarts.
4) Sidecar/envoy config mismatch on canary replicas (wrong configmap version picked up).

Things tried (and results):
- Forced pod restart for all canary pods: kubectl delete pod -l release=canary-v2025-02-14 -n prod -> pods recreated and some nodes failed to pull for ~30s but then OK. No lasting improvement.
- Manual traffic shift using flagger/traffic-split CLI: set canary weight 0 -> one node still showed requests to canary (checked request logs with X-Request-Id)
- Redeployed stable image explicitly by digest on canary replicaset: patched deployment image to gcr.io/redwood/release@sha256:00ff33... -> stabilized latency. This suggests tag ambiguity.

Evidence pointing at tag/digest mismatch:
- docker inspect digest != image referenced in some pod descriptions during window.
- GCR build log shows two pushes within 30s (build 1234 and 1235) with same tag but different digests (CI race).

Short-term remediation performed:
- Manually pinned canary replicaset to stable digest and scaled canary down to 0.
- Opened rollback PR to ensure deploy job pins by digest for canaries: PR #987 (linked).
- Notified SRE + Pod infra in #deploys; added note to hold further canary rollouts until CI fixes tag reuse.

Next steps / action items (prioritized):
- CI: stop reusing tags for consecutive builds; use unique tag pattern (timestamp+sha) and ensure deploy reads digest from GCR API before applying. (owner: ci-team, Jira RDW-3421).
- Release infra: add pre-deploy check that reads repo digest and compares across nodes (owner: eng-release-engineering).
- Investigate code path causing nil pointer in kv_cache.go: add additional logging and a canary-only flag to enable heavy tracing (owner: serving-runtime team, ticket assigned).
- Add draining validation to the canary controller: verify no active sessions for the canary before final ejection.

Hand-off notes for follow-up:
- If someone picks this up, start by reading the build logs in cloud-build (linked). Confirm whether any other builds that day reused tags.
- Check cluster node images cache: ssh into node that failed pulls (kubelet logs archived) -> path: /var/log/kubelet.log on node ip 10.20.30.40 (SRE has creds).

Questions I still have (unresolved):
- Why did autoscaler/flagger allow ejection while sessions remained pinned? Is the ingress affinity header being honored?
- Was there any canary-specific configmap change in the same deploy? (I didn't see one in Helm diff but need to confirm).

Dirty TODOs (quick):
- [ ] Attach paused CI build artifact list to RDW-3421.
- [ ] Add test that asserts image tag immutability for deploy pipeline.
- [ ] Postmortem skeleton (owner: me) and link to RDW-3421 when ready.

Random operator commands I might need later:
- gcloud container images list-tags gcr.io/redwood/release --limit=50 --format=json | jq '.[] | {tags: .tags, digest: .digest}'
- kubectl get svc frontend -o yaml | yq '.spec.sessionAffinity'

End notes: keep this as personal scratchpad until we have CI fix confirmed. Will convert into short incident summary for postmortem once code/digest root cause is confirmed.
